highlights: every dataset lists its variables in an order drawn from its seed, with the true graph permuted the same way, so the column order carries nothing of the causal order
GIES, exact search, CD-NOD, MultiGroupDirectLiNGAM, GFCI, GIN, and CALM measured against their reference packages
GES's scoring engine measured against the 0.4.0 build on the same datasets

andrey_builds.build: pre-release Andrey 0.7.0 build, 19 October 2026, with order-free possible-d-separation

andrey_source: every method runs the build of 17 October 2026 except GIN, which ran on the build of 18 October 2026, whose GIN root test runs once per cluster member and whose search follows each column's data; CD-NOD, whose Andrey rows ran on the build of 19 October 2026, whose Meek and FCI orientation rules run in order-free rounds; and GFCI (with its FCI and parallel side rows), whose Andrey rows ran on the build of 19 October 2026 with order-free possible-d-separation, which also visits the possible-d-separation step's pairs, nodes, and subsets in a rank computed from each column's data; GIN's reference packages ran with the same harness and data on the build of 16 October 2026, Tetrad's GFCI and causal-learn's CD-NOD on the build of 17 October 2026. The 0.4.0 rows run the released Andrey 0.4.0 on the same datasets

GIES.name: interventional_gauss_er
GIES.description: linear-Gaussian data that mixes observation with interventions, simulated as in Hauser and Buhlmann (2012, Section 5.2.1): a random DAG in which each pair of variables is an edge with probability 2 / (d - 1) (mean degree 2), in a uniformly random causal order; edge weights uniform on [-1, -0.1] or [0.1, 1] and error variances uniform on [0.5, 1], rescaled so every variable has unit variance without interventions; round(0.4 d) single-variable intervention targets drawn at random, each target's rows setting its variable from N(2, 0.2^2); 10 d rows, split evenly between no intervention and each target. Each fit gets the samples and the rows' intervention targets.

Exact search.name: linear_gauss_er
Exact search.description: linear-Gaussian data on an Erdos-Renyi DAG with mean degree 2, standardized, with n = 10 d rows. The variables are listed in an order drawn from the dataset's seed, with the true graph permuted the same way, so the column order carries nothing of the causal order.

MultiGroupDirectLiNGAM.name: multi_group_er
MultiGroupDirectLiNGAM.description: three groups of n = 1000 rows over the same d variables: one Erdos-Renyi DAG with mean degree 2 for all groups, linear with uniform noise, weights with |w| uniform on [0.5, 2] and a random sign drawn for each group, every variable rescaled to unit variance in causal order. The groups are given side by side; the truth is the block-diagonal DAG of the groups' copies. The variables are, in every group, listed in an order drawn from the dataset's seed, with the true graph permuted the same way, so the column order carries nothing of the causal order.

GFCI.name: latent_gauss_er
GFCI.description: linear-Gaussian data on an Erdos-Renyi DAG with mean degree 2, standardized, with one node in ten hidden and n = 10 d rows; d counts the hidden nodes, and each dataset has d - d / 10 data columns ('observed'). The truth is the PAG of the observed variables. The variables are listed in an order drawn from the dataset's seed, with the true graph permuted the same way, so the column order carries nothing of the causal order.

GIN.name: latent_measurement
GIN.description: m latent variables, each a cause of every later one, each measured by three observed indicators of its own; linear with uniform noise, loadings and weights with |w| uniform on [0.5, 2] and a random sign, every variable rescaled to unit variance; n = 1000 rows of the 3 m indicators. d counts the latents and their indicators ('observed' the indicators). The indicators come in a uniformly random column order, so the column order carries nothing of the clusters or the latents' order.

CALM.name: linear_gauss_er
CALM.description: linear-Gaussian data on an Erdos-Renyi DAG with mean degree 2, standardized, with n = 10 d rows. The variables are listed in an order drawn from the dataset's seed, with the true graph permuted the same way, so the column order carries nothing of the causal order.

CALM, paper schedule.name: linear_gauss_er
CALM, paper schedule.description: linear-Gaussian data on an Erdos-Renyi DAG with mean degree 2, standardized, with n = 10 d rows. The variables are listed in an order drawn from the dataset's seed, with the true graph permuted the same way, so the column order carries nothing of the causal order.

CD-NOD.name: domain_shift_er
CD-NOD.description: a linear-Gaussian Erdos-Renyi DAG with mean degree 2, every variable rescaled to unit variance in causal order, with n = 2000 rows pooled from four domains in equal blocks; one variable in three, at least one, shifts its mean with the domain, by s k / 3 standard deviations in domain k, s uniform on [0.5, 1.5]. The truth is the CPDAG CD-NOD can identify: the domain index orients the edges it reaches. The variables are listed in an order drawn from the dataset's seed, with the true graph permuted the same way, so the column order carries nothing of the causal order.

methods.comparator_setting: score='GaussL0penIntScore', lambda_rule='0.5*log(n)', intercept=True, max_degree=None, phase=['forward', 'backward', 'turning'], iterate=True
methods.note: pcalg's gies maximizes GaussL0penIntScore with its default penalty lambda = 0.5 log(n), BIC in log-likelihood units, the objective Andrey's gies minimizes at lambda_value=1 in deviance units, with intercept=TRUE, as Andrey centers each variable on the rows it is scored on. Both run the forward, backward, and turning phases until none improves, with no degree cap, and both return the interventional essential graph. pcalg runs in an embedded R session; its timed region holds the conversion of the rows' intervention sets into pcalg's targets and target index
methods.error_metric: SHD between the estimated interventional essential graph and the true DAG's, under the same intervention targets: one per variable pair whose edge differs (missing, extra, or oriented differently). The empty graph's SHD is the number of true edges.
methods.fit_protocol: one fit at a time on an exclusive node, 4 cores per fit, 1 timed repeat and 1 warm-up fit per dataset, a 1800 s wall cap covering the warm-up and the timed fit, and a 30000 MB memory cap per fit
methods.same_graph_test: the same essential graph: equal endpoint marks

methods.note: Both run A* for a DAG with the lowest BIC, with no parent cap; causal-learn's optimal path extension does not change the optimum. methods.note: Tetrad is the causal-cmd 1.12.0 jar (tetrad-lib 7.6.3). Tetrad runs through a small Java driver that times the search call inside the JVM, after its warm-up searches in the same JVM; the whole process, with the JVM start, the driver's compile, and the CSV round trip, is recorded apart and not used. The JVM sees only the fit's cores. Its settings: fisher-z-test at alpha 0.05, sem-bic-score with penaltyDiscount 1 (Andrey's lambda_value), no structure prior (semBicStructurePrior 0), the standard penalty rule (semBicRule 1), no depth or path-length cap, the possible-d-separation step, the discriminating-path rule and the complete rule set R1-R10, causal-cmd's degree cap of 1,000, which no graph here reaches, and a precomputed covariance matrix, which changes its speed, not its answer. Beside each row: Andrey's FCI (Fisher-Z at alpha 0.05) on the same datasets (fci_*), the test-only search GFCI improves on; and Andrey's GFCI run with its GES step in the fit's four cores as worker processes (andrey_parallel_*), which returns the same PAG; andrey_parallel_ratio is the one-process time over the parallel time, below 1 where the parallel mode is slower. Andrey's GFCI and FCI ran on the build of 19 October 2026 with order-free possible-d-separation, whose orientation rules run in order-free rounds: every rule reads the graph as the round starts, an edge or endpoint the rules decide both ways stays undirected or a circle, and the rounds repeat to a fixed point, whose GFCI keeps every smallest separating set it finds rather than the first in column order, and whose possible-d-separation step (possible_dsep='order_free', the default) visits the pairs, the nodes of each search, and the subsets in a tie rank computed from each column's own data rather than in column order; Tetrad's fits and the empty graph ran on the build of 17 October 2026 with the same harness and data, so their records stand
methods.error_metric: endpoint SHD between the estimated PAG and the true PAG of the observed variables: one per edge endpoint whose mark differs (tail, arrowhead, or circle), so a missing or extra edge counts its two endpoints and a reversed directed edge counts two. The empty graph's is twice the true PAG's edge count.

methods.fit_protocol: one fit at a time on an exclusive node, 4 cores per fit, 1 timed repeat and 1 warm-up fit per dataset, a 1800 s wall cap covering the warm-up and the timed fit, and a 30000 MB memory cap per fit
methods.same_graph_test: the same PAG: endpoint SHD 0 between the two packages' PAGs

methods.note: Tetrad's GIN comes from tetrad-lib 7.6.10, which no causal-cmd release bundles. Tetrad runs through a small Java driver that times the search call inside the JVM, after its warm-up searches in the same JVM; the whole process, with the JVM start, the driver's compile, and the CSV round trip, is recorded apart and not used. The JVM sees only the fit's cores. Tetrad's GIN takes a raw marginal independence test; it runs Tetrad's KCI under its defaults, a Gaussian kernel with a median-distance bandwidth and the gamma approximation, the family of the gamma-HSIC test Andrey's GIN runs, each with its own bandwidth rule, so the two can decide a test differently at alpha 0.05. Andrey's GIN ran on the build of 18 October 2026, whose root test runs once per cluster member, whose search follows each column's data rather than its position, and which builds each column's kernel matrix once per fit; the reference packages' fits ran on the build of 16 October 2026 with the same GIN harness and data (its regime draws a random column order of its own and takes no shuffle step), so their records stand. Its sizes are latent counts m = 2, 3, 4: d counts the latents and their indicators, 'observed' the 3 m indicators
methods.error_metric: GIN returns a cluster of indicators per latent and an order of the latents, scored against the truth: cluster_ari, the adjusted Rand index of the two clusterings of the indicators (an unclustered indicator is a cluster of its own); clusters_found, the share of true clusters the estimate has exactly; order_accuracy, over the pairs of true latents whose clusters it has exactly, the share it orders as the truth does (no value when it has fewer than two); latents_found, the latents it returns. The error count, latents_missed, is the number of true latents whose indicators it does not return as one cluster. The empty graph finds no cluster: ARI 0, no cluster found, every latent missed.
methods.fit_protocol: one fit at a time on an exclusive node, 4 cores per fit, 1 timed repeat and 0 warm-up fits per dataset, a 1800 s wall cap covering the warm-up and the timed fit, and a 30000 MB memory cap per fit
methods.same_graph_test: the same clusters and the same latent graph: equal structure hashes

methods.note: causal-learn 0.1.4.8's GIN with indep_test_method='hsic', its gamma-approximation HSIC test, the test Andrey's GIN runs, with one fix applied: in both search phases its GIN tests the residual against the column at each loop counter (range(len(...))) instead of the column of each variable it names, so it tests the wrong columns whenever the remaining variables are not the first ones; the fix indexes the data by the variable (py-why/causal-learn issue 271). A cluster it cannot order is in its graph only, read as a latent pointing into its members. Andrey's GIN ran on the build of 18 October 2026, whose root test runs once per cluster member, whose search follows each column's data rather than its position, and which builds each column's kernel matrix once per fit; the reference packages' fits ran on the build of 16 October 2026 with the same GIN harness and data (its regime draws a random column order of its own and takes no shuffle step), so their records stand. Its sizes are latent counts m = 2, 3, 4: d counts the latents and their indicators, 'observed' the 3 m indicators
methods.error_metric: GIN returns a cluster of indicators per latent and an order of the latents, scored against the truth: cluster_ari, the adjusted Rand index of the two clusterings of the indicators (an unclustered indicator is a cluster of its own); clusters_found, the share of true clusters the estimate has exactly; order_accuracy, over the pairs of true latents whose clusters it has exactly, the share it orders as the truth does (no value when it has fewer than two); latents_found, the latents it returns. The error count, latents_missed, is the number of true latents whose indicators it does not return as one cluster. The empty graph finds no cluster: ARI 0, no cluster found, every latent missed.

methods.comparator_setting: alpha=0.05, indep_test='fisherz', n_domains=4, stable=True, uc_priority=2, uc_rule=0
methods.note: Both run Fisher-Z at alpha 0.05 with a stable skeleton search and rebuild the domain index from the rows (four domains). Andrey orients the index's edges first and ranks the colliders by the p-values that separated their ends (collider_order='p_value', its default); causal-learn (uc_rule=0, uc_priority=2) puts a collider wherever the middle node is in no separating set, in the order it visits the triples, and skips one that would reverse an edge already directed. The two rules agree unless wrong independence decisions make two colliders conflict; then each keeps a different one, so same_graph compares two collider rules. Andrey's graph does not depend on the column order: the collider step is order-free, and so are Meek's rules. Andrey's CD-NOD ran on the build of 19 October 2026, whose orientation rules run in order-free rounds: every rule reads the graph as the round starts, an edge or endpoint the rules decide both ways stays undirected or a circle, and the rounds repeat to a fixed point; causal-learn's fits and the empty graph ran on the build of 17 October 2026 with the same harness and data, so their records stand
methods.error_metric: SHD between the estimate and the CPDAG CD-NOD can identify, in which the domain index orients the edges it reaches: one per variable pair whose edge differs (missing, extra, or oriented differently). The empty graph's SHD is the number of true edges.
